claim: loginctl enable-linger spawns a user manager at boot and keeps it around after logouts, letting users who are not logged in run long-running services; mechanically it just creates an empty file at /var/lib/systemd/linger/USER
stance_target: lingering is the prerequisite for headless user-scoped agent deployment
quoted_support: enable-linger spawns a user manager at boot and keeps it around after logouts, letting users who are not logged in run long-running services; mechanically it just creates an empty file at /var/lib/systemd/linger/USER

claim: A declarative NixOS workaround for enabling lingering without a dedicated option (as of June 2023) is systemd.tmpfiles.rules = [ "f /var/lib/systemd/linger/alice" ... ], i.e. declaratively creating the linger file via tmpfiles
stance_target: jupiterOS fleet config can declaratively enable linger for the agent user while awaiting the first-class option
scope_conditions: NixOS; predates/absence of a first-class linger option (nixpkgs issue #3702 still open)
quoted_support: rnhmjoj's interim workaround (6 likes): systemd.tmpfiles.rules = [ "f /var/lib/systemd/linger/alice" ... ] — declaratively creating the linger file without a dedicated option

claim: Named use-cases for lingering on headless servers: running Syncthing via home-manager when no one is logged in, and rootless Docker/podman containers that must stay up without a login session
stance_target: lingering is an established pattern for headless user-scoped daemons beyond the agent use-case
quoted_support: Use-cases named: headless servers running Syncthing via home-manager when no one is logged in, and rootless Docker/podman containers that must stay up without a login session.

claim: Counter-position: for headless servers without interactive users, run the daemon as a system service (a NixOS module, or virtualisation.oci-containers with DynamicUser=yes) instead of using lingering user services
stance_target: lingered user services as the fleet-wide agent mechanism on headless jupiterOS hosts
scope_conditions: headless servers without interactive users; NixOS
quoted_support: Counter-position from peterhoeg: for headless servers without interactive users, run the daemon as a system service (nixos module, or virtualisation.oci-containers with DynamicUser=yes) instead of lingering user services.
